title: Finite powers of a regular sheaf are projective on a weakly contractible scheme
statement: Let S be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] whose terminal small pro-etale object is weakly contractible [sk-def-pe-weak-contractible]. For any sheaf of rings R on this site [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and any natural number n, the product of n copies of the regular R-module sheaf is projective: every map from this product lifts across every epimorphism of R-module sheaves. The case n=0 is included.

proof.text: The regular-module Hom equivalence identifies a map from R with the image of 1 as a compatible global section. Forgetting modules preserves epimorphisms by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful]. The sheaf epimorphism criterion makes this a locally surjective map of set sheaves. Weak contractibility lifts its prescribed terminal section. Restrict the lift to every object; compatibility gives a module morphism. Naturality shows its composite equals the original morphism.

Finite products are finite biproducts. For a map out of a finite biproduct, lift its composite with each coprojection by the regular-module result, then assemble the lifts by biproduct.desc. Extensionality on coprojections proves the factorization. Transfer projectivity across the product-biproduct isomorphism. The empty biproduct is covered by the same argument.
